personas.name: Dr. Amina Patel
goals: Create and manage billable-hours drafts for selected date ranges aligned to configured funder reporting periods
Review how Outlook events and GitHub activity are mapped to each project/sub-case with clear confidence and non-technical explanations
Edit suggested hours and add notes for deviations while tracking deltas from system suggestions
Identify and resolve unmapped or low-confidence time candidates
Mark the draft as ready only after review and export in funder-specific Excel formats they trust
frustrations: Having suggestions that feel like surveillance or productivity scoring rather than transparent time attribution
Mappings that are unclear, lack rationale/confidence, or silently omit unmapped items
Suggested totals that don’t match their expectations, forcing time-consuming back-and-forth
Export fields/totals that don’t reflect their edits or that fail validation without a clear message
Slow or blocker-heavy UI steps that prevent completing the workflow quickly (target ≤15 minutes)

personas.name: Marco Rossi
goals: Monitor ingestion status for each user/source (Outlook and GitHub) and quickly diagnose failures
Troubleshoot and retry failed ingestion jobs (e.g., credentials/API limits) without breaking user configurations
Maintain project/repository linking heuristics and override mechanisms to support flexible mapping
Update export mapping configuration so funder outputs match required column/row structures
Support pilot evaluation by ensuring traceability summaries and coverage/low-confidence handling behave as specified
frustrations: Ingestion failures that don’t provide actionable error categories and next steps
Operational dashboards/logs that are hard to interpret during a time-boxed pilot
Export mapping changes that require code changes instead of configuration updates
Unclear whether a user’s draft issue is due to ingestion, mapping heuristics, or export validation
Difficulty verifying what was stored/derived because of insufficient data inventory/retention visibility

personas.name: Sofia Nguyen
goals: Ensure RBAC and pilot policy restrictions are enforced (researchers can’t access others’ drafts or mappings)
Oversee privacy controls: minimum stored fields, configurable retention with an upper bound, and auditability via summary trace links
Confirm export generation requires explicit researcher readiness marking and blocks premature exports
Validate that funder-specific exports conform (totals match draft within required granularity and columns are present)
Support pilot success metrics and usability outcomes without compromising non-surveillance intent
frustrations: Access-control bugs that could expose another researcher’s attribution drafts or mapping details
Uncertainty about what data is stored versus ingested and whether retention/anonymization policies are actually working
Exports being generated or used without explicit researcher review/ready marking
Lack of transparency for coordinators when validation fails (e.g., why totals/columns don’t conform)
Too much technical jargon in explanations or UI language that undermines the non-surveillance rationale
